Why this National union page differs
Provenance precedes performance because cross-centre deduplication defines the national denominator. The field view uses SJR areas/categories for every record; WoS/JCR categories remain on WoS-only pages so two taxonomies are never mixed. Researcher evidence uses one Scopus-anchored national list; WoS papers are unioned only for a non-conflicting exact ORCID plus compatible name, while unmatched identities remain in source audit views.
Two centres, one national count. TRUBA (TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM) and UHeM (İstanbul Technical University) are, as far as this project is aware, the two HPC centres serving Turkish research at national scale -- this page is the union of their acknowledgment corpora, each itself already a Scopus+WoS union (see the per-centre combined pages). If a third national or regional centre exists, it is not tracked here, and this total should be read as "the two centres we track", not "all of Turkish HPC".

302 papers acknowledge both centres and are counted once here, not twice -- simply adding TRUBA's 2,837 and UHeM's 859 would overstate the national total by exactly that many. Quartiles are SCImago SJR throughout (not the WoS/JCR table used on the WoS-only pages), matching every other combined page on this site. Open access is on OpenAIRE's definition here — gold, hybrid, bronze, green or diamond, looked up by DOI over every article in this corpus — because this page carries that colour and OpenAIRE sees repository copies that Scopus's and WoS's publisher-side flags do not. The per-database dashboards keep those native flags and therefore report a lower share; the breakdown below shows the whole distribution. Click any tile, bar, or chart segment below for a quick paper list, or use the full national paper table below.

What each database contributes

WoS-only 522
Retrieval gaps affect high-impact work. Among the ten most-cited articles here, 5 entered this corpus only through the Web of Science source arm and 2 only through the Scopus source arm. Each arm is acknowledgment-defined and can include reviewed paper-level evidence. “Only” does not necessarily mean the article is absent from the other database, whose funding metadata may differ. The single most-cited article in this corpus — Two- and One-Dimensional Honeycomb Structures of Silicon and Germanium (2009, 3,060 citations) — entered this acknowledgment corpus only through the Web of Science source arm; a Scopus acknowledgment-only study would omit it.

Open-access colour (OpenAIRE, enriched over the whole union)

gold/hybrid/bronze/green/diamond from the OpenAIRE Graph, looked up by DOI across every article in this combined corpus (Scopus and WoS-only alike) — 3,349 of 3,394 matched.
The headline "Open access (OpenAIRE)" tile above is this breakdown: everything except Closed. 45 articles have no DOI match in OpenAIRE and fall back to the Scopus/WoS native flag, the only signal left for them.

Why the per-database pages report a much lower share. Scopus's openaccess flag and WoS's journal_oas_gold are publisher-side: they see the version of record, not a repository deposit. On this corpus they call 869 articles open where OpenAIRE calls 2,208 open, and green — 1,055 papers here — is most of that difference. Neither number is wrong; they answer different questions, so this page states which one it is using.

Identity rule. Cross-source linking requires an exact ORCID and compatible surname/given-name evidence. The build rejected 31 ORCID value(s) attached to incompatible names rather than forcing a merge. WoS identities that cannot be tied safely to a Turkish-affiliated anchor remain in the source-specific audit lists above; this conservative rule may split a person, but it does not merge homonyms or treat every foreign coauthor as a Turkish researcher.

Browse all 3,394 articles

Searches titles, journals, years and DOIs across the entire deduplicated corpus. Centre filters include papers credited to both centres where appropriate; database provenance reports which index found the record.
Click a column heading to sort.
Method. Union of TRUBA's and UHeM's Scopus+WoS acknowledgment corpora (journal articles only), merged on DOI (or a normalised title for the handful without one). A paper acknowledging both centres is counted once. Citations are the higher of the two databases' counts, never the sum. Quartiles, broad areas and detailed fields are SCImago SJR throughout. OA colour is OpenAIRE's, by DOI, over the whole corpus. Institution, country and field summaries use whole counting, so a multi-institution, multi-country or multi-category paper can contribute once to each applicable group.

Reading the early years. Web of Science began indexing funding-acknowledgment text in August 2008. Earlier papers carry none at all, so no acknowledgment search can reach them whatever the wording — in this snapshot 0.8% of 2007 records hold any funding text, against 9.9% in 2008 and 28–38% from 2009 onward. Pre-2008 work appears here only where the record was loaded years after publication. Sparse early years are a property of the index, not evidence that little was acknowledged. Before 2008 this national total rests on the Scopus arm alone, apart from a few WoS records loaded retrospectively — which is why the earliest entry here is a WoS-only 2005 article rather than anything Scopus returns.

Important interpretation. Large source-level citation differences do not by themselves show a citation-counting error: Scopus and WoS retrieve different acknowledgment-defined paper sets, and a small number of highly cited source-exclusive papers can dominate a year. The repository findings log records worked DOI-level checks, including the tested absence of WLCG collaboration papers from the direct TRUBA acknowledgment corpus. WLCG is excluded from this national total because its attribution method is collaboration membership rather than centre acknowledgment.

Personal research project — not an official TÜBİTAK, ULAKBİM or İTÜ website.
